detail: measured is the FITTED alpha (0.683 [0.642, 0.963]  (systematic [0.683, 0.963]: activation-corrected to fixed-cost-corrected; bootstrap [0.642, 0.727] over 400 resamples of 16 treads)), measured at BLOCK_M=64 over 16 memory-bound treads, activation traffic subtracted. It is not a crossing ratio and no crossing was measured to produce it.
the interval is DISJOINT from the band and lies ABOVE it: measured 0.683 [0.642, 0.963] is ABOVE the band [0.529, 0.588]

INFORMATIONAL, the retired one-sided gate: alpha > 0.33 would have read PASS. It is not the verdict: it passes for everything from 0.33 to 1.0, so it cannot fail from above and every committed surface fit clears it.
NO ladder's fitted slopes imply a crossing exists (C > B is met nowhere; slopes missing at [256]), so nothing here is a crossing measurement and no crossing has been observed

the same alpha restates the model's crossing ratio as 1 + 0.683 = 1.683x, which is what the retired ratio gate printed as its 'measured' value. That number is algebra over this line, not a second observation.
model's crossing ratio: ridge 145.8: no crossing   ridge 158.6: no crossing

ALPHA_BY_BLOCK_M records a drift of about +/-25% across block sizes, and that drift is `phi` growing with BM/BN rather than a different miss fraction, so an imported alpha is an alpha of ANOTHER TILING and the import is a bound, not a substitution.

gates.claim: BLOCK_M=64 never reaches the compute roof (ridge x bandwidth)
gates.gate: < 0.95 of ridge x bandwidth, and <= 0.868 (the midpoint of this run's ceiling 0.736 and the rival world's 1.000)
detail: THE SWEEP IS NOT BRACKETED, so an absence here is not evidence of absence and this gate refuses to score it.
measured in fractions of ridge x bandwidth (682 TFLOP/s); the refit caps this block size at cap/ridge = 114.7/155.9 = 0.736 and the retracted alpha=0.1 at 1.000

this arm's own plateau is 367.6 TFLOP/s = 53.9% of that roof. Against the plateau this block size peaks at 0.824, which is the number the retired gate scored against 0.85. It is ARM-RELATIVE and it is not the verdict.
per-tile slopes: memory B=0.7398 ms against compute C=0.6199 ms (scaled from the reference by C ~ BLOCK_M). C > B is the condition for a crossing to exist at all, and it is NOT met.
swept to 1024 rows per expert (16 M-tiles)
horizon 374 rows: 2x the crossing the retracted alpha=0.1 predicts for this block size
positive control: NOTHING reached the compute roof in this grid (best other block size 0.54 of ridge x bandwidth = 682 TFLOP/s), so the sweep never demonstrated it can detect a crossing at all
modelled AI at the last tread is 95.3% of the ceiling, and the last tread gained 2.9% of throughput over the one before it
